edges.rationale: Block and stream ciphers are modern symmetric techniques that presuppose the shared-secret-key model and classical cipher concepts (substitution, key usage) introduced in the basics.
CBC is a mode of operation on block ciphers; understanding what a block cipher is and how independent block encryption leaks patterns is necessary to see why chaining with an IV is used.

Public key cryptography is defined in explicit contrast with the shared-secret model, including how a shared key implicitly identifies the sender — this comparison requires the symmetric model as a baseline.
RSA is a concrete instantiation of the two-key public/private model; key generation and its use as a public encryption scheme only make sense after the public key model is established.
